question: Can you upgrade a wastewater plant's switchgear?
html:
Yes. Electrical work at wastewater plants and pump stations is a core focus for us, led by Horton Electrical Services in Connecticut (CET growth plan). Equipment ratings, outage windows and schedule for a specific switchgear scope are set plant by plant after a site review.

What we bring to a plant

  • Wastewater relationships. Horton joined CET in September 2026 and brings Connecticut wastewater relationships (CET growth plan).
  • Electrical plus efficiency. We pair Horton's electrical work with NuWave's energy-efficiency work. Aeration, often a plant's biggest energy load, is a natural fit (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • Regional reach. CET holds licenses in six states, including CT, MA and RI (CET growth plan).
  • Bigger plants. At sites like MWRA Deer Island, which already generates 26% of its own power, our role is electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency (CET wastewater-plant targets).

Where upgrade work is funded

These are public funding-list items and requests. They are not CET contracts (CET wastewater-plant targets).

PlantFunded or listed projectOther requests
New Haven East Shore STP (40 MGD)$82M wet-weather and odor-control upgrade, CT FY27 fundable list$19.2M process-air compressors
Hartford WPCF (60 MGD)$24.3M sludge screening and equalization, fundable FY26-27$31.6M Island Road and Hog Brook pump stations
Norwalk WPCF (18 MGD)$26M final-settling-tank upgrade, fundable FY27$48M green aeration system
  • Our target list counts 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects across CT, MA and RI (CET growth plan).
  • Only CT Table 2 / Category I items are on the fundable list. Table 3 items are requests, and the RI list is a June 2026 draft (CET wastewater-plant targets).

What we don't yet know

The data does not show switchgear age, ratings or replacement plans at any plant. That scope would come from:

  • the plant's electrical one-line drawings and equipment inventory
  • load and metering data, especially for aeration and pump stations
  • the bid documents for the funded project

Wastewater electrical work is the main Phase 1 lever in the growth plan. It is also the entry point for SCADA and pump-station monitoring contracts, the recurring service mix that buyers price well above project-only contractors (CET growth plan).

Next actions

  1. Ask New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk for electrical one-lines and equipment lists tied to their funded projects.
  2. Check each listed project's bid scope for switchgear, MCC or service-entrance work before committing estimating time.
  3. Draft a joint Horton and NuWave proposal for Norwalk's aeration request, covering electrical and efficiency together.
  4. Refresh the target list against the Oct 7, 2026 EPA wastewater-plant compliance snapshot so plant data stays current.
